standard_prerequisites: the Bondal-Van den Bergh theorem producing a perfect K-injective generator of D_QCoh(O_X) for quasi-compact quasi-separated X
K-injective complexes and the identification of dga cohomology with Ext groups
the dga tensor functor - tensor^L_E K and its adjoint RHom(K, -)
compactness of perfect objects and the fully-faithfulness criterion of the tensor functor in the compact case
the generator property and the formal equivalence criterion for an adjunction whose restricted kernel vanishes
core_obligations: Prove that for quasi-compact quasi-separated X there is a dga (E,d) with finitely many nonzero cohomology groups such that D_QCoh(O_X) is equivalent to D(E,d)
proof_roadmap: Pick a perfect K-injective generator K of D_QCoh(O_X) and take E = the dga of endomorphisms of K in the dg category of complexes
K-injectivity identifies H^n(E) with Ext^n(K,K), only finitely many of which are nonzero since K is perfect and the cohomologies of a generator are bounded
The tensor functor D(E,d) to D(O_X) is fully faithful by the compactness of K and the finite-Ext computation, and has RHom(K,-) as right adjoint, a left quasi-inverse by adjunction generalities
The tensor functor lands in D_QCoh by the tensor-with-QCoh-complex lemma, and the restricted adjunction kernel vanishes because K generates D_QCoh
The formal adjunction criterion with vanishing kernel upgrades fully faithfulness plus left quasi-inverse to an equivalence with D_QCoh(O_X)
difficulty_reason: H2: a generator-and-adjunction argument; the source assembles five quoted ingredients and states the formal conclusion, all steps being present though several are by reference.
